:::{#exr-solve-normal-equations}
#### Solving the normal equations

Using @exr-rss-deriv-intercept and @exr-rss-deriv-slope,
solve the normal equations of @exm-normal-equations-slr
for $\intcoef$ and $\coef{x}$,
assuming $\sspred > 0$ (@def-centered-sums).
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-solve-normal-equations}

**First normal equation.**
Set the derivative from @exr-rss-deriv-intercept to zero,
then isolate $\intcoef$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= -2 \paren{n \outbar - n \intcoef - \coef{x} n \predbar}
&& \text{(first normal equation)}\\
0 &= n \outbar - n \intcoef - \coef{x} n \predbar
&& \text{(divide both sides by $-2$)}\\
0 &= \outbar - \intcoef - \coef{x} \predbar
&& \text{(divide both sides by $n$)}\\
\intcoef &= \outbar - \coef{x} \predbar
&& \text{(add $\intcoef$ to both sides)}
\end{aligned}
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

**Second normal equation.**
Substitute that intercept into the derivative from @exr-rss-deriv-slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial \text{RSS}}{\partial \coef{x}}
&= -2 \sumin \predvar_\iobs (\outvar_\iobs - \intcoef - \coef{x} \predvar_\iobs)
&& \text{(derivative with respect to $\coef{x}$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin \predvar_\iobs \paren{\outvar_\iobs - (\outbar - \coef{x} \predbar) - \coef{x} \predvar_\iobs}
&& \text{(substitute $\intcoef$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin \predvar_\iobs \paren{\outvar_\iobs - \outbar + \coef{x} \predbar - \coef{x} \predvar_\iobs}
&& \text{(remove the inner parentheses)}\\
&= -2 \sumin \predvar_\iobs \paren{(\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - (\coef{x} \predvar_\iobs - \coef{x} \predbar)}
&& \text{(group terms)}\\
&= -2 \sumin \predvar_\iobs \paren{(\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \coef{x} (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)}
&& \text{(factor out $\coef{x}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

To shorten the next steps, write
$d_i \eqdef (\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \coef{x} (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)$,
so that $\partial \text{RSS} / \partial \coef{x} = -2 \sumin \predvar_\iobs d_i$.
The $d_i$ sum to zero,
because deviations from a sample mean sum to zero (@exr-sum-deviations-zero):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sumin d_i
&= \sumin \paren{(\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \coef{x} (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)}
&& \text{(definition of $d_i$)}\\
&= \sumin (\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \sumin \coef{x} (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)
&& \text{(split the sum)}\\
&= \sumin (\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \coef{x} \sumin (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)
&& \text{(constant factor out of the sum)}\\
&= 0 - \coef{x} \cdot 0
&& \text{(deviations sum to zero)}\\
&= 0 - 0
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= 0
&& \text{(subtract)}
\end{aligned}
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

So subtracting $\predbar \sumin d_i$ from $\sumin \predvar_\iobs d_i$
does not change it:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sumin \predvar_\iobs d_i
&= \sumin \predvar_\iobs d_i - \predbar \sumin d_i
&& \text{($\sumin d_i = 0$)}\\
&= \sumin \predvar_\iobs d_i - \sumin \predbar d_i
&& \text{(constant factor into the sum)}\\
&= \sumin (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar) d_i
&& \text{(combine the sums)}\\
&= \sumin (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar) \paren{(\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \coef{x} (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)}
&& \text{(definition of $d_i$)}\\
&= \sumin \paren{(\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)(\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \coef{x} (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)^2}
&& \text{(distribute)}\\
&= \sumin (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)(\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \sumin \coef{x} (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)^2
&& \text{(split the sum)}\\
&= \sumin (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)(\outvar_\iobs - \outbar) - \coef{x} \sumin (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)^2
&& \text{(constant factor out of the sum)}\\
&= \sspredout - \coef{x} \sumin (\predvar_\iobs - \predbar)^2
&& \text{(definition of $\sspredout$)}\\
&= \sspredout - \coef{x} \sspred
&& \text{(definition of $\sspred$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $\partial \text{RSS} / \partial \coef{x} = -2 \paren{\sspredout - \coef{x} \sspred}$.
Set it to zero and isolate $\coef{x}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= -2 \paren{\sspredout - \coef{x} \sspred}
&& \text{(second normal equation)}\\
0 &= \sspredout - \coef{x} \sspred
&& \text{(divide both sides by $-2$)}\\
\coef{x} \sspred &= \sspredout
&& \text{(add $\coef{x} \sspred$ to both sides)}\\
\coef{x} &= \frac{\sspredout}{\sspred}
&& \text{(divide both sides by $\sspred > 0$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So the normal equations have exactly one solution:
$\coef{x} = \sspredout / \sspred$ and $\intcoef = \outbar - \coef{x} \predbar$.

:::
